- Always verify the signature before processing the payload.
- Use HTTPS endpoints only.
- Treat the payload as untrusted input; validate and sanitise as you would any external data.
- Do not log full payloads if they contain personal data; log the event id and type instead.

The dashboard provides a “Send test event” button. You can also use the command-line tool supplied in the SDK to replay recorded events against a local listener.

If you encounter persistent delivery problems, open a ticket with the event id and the approximate time of the failure. Do not include your signing secret in the ticket.

Post-incident review – INC-2026-1030-002

Summary
On 30 October between 14:02 and 14:47 UTC the checkout service returned elevated 503 errors. Approximately 2.3 % of checkout attempts failed. Revenue impact was estimated at $18 k.

Root cause
A configuration change that increased the database connection-pool size was applied without a corresponding increase in the database’s max_connections setting. When traffic rose after a marketing email, the pool exhausted the available database connections and new requests queued until they timed out.

Detection
The existing latency and error-rate alerts fired within two minutes. The on-call engineer acknowledged at 14:05.

Mitigation
The connection-pool setting was reverted at 14:18. Error rates began to decline immediately and returned to baseline by 14:47. A subsequent change raised the database max_connections value in a controlled manner.

Lessons learned
- Configuration changes that affect resource limits must be paired with a check of the downstream dependency’s limits.
- The change-management template has been updated to include an explicit “downstream capacity” checkbox.
- A synthetic checkout probe that runs every minute has been added so that future degradations are detected even if the error-rate alert is slow.

Action items
- Update the runbook (owner: platform team, due 15 Nov)
- Add the downstream-capacity check to the CI lint rules (owner: infra, due 22 Nov)
- Review other services for similar pool-versus-max_connections mismatches (owner: backend guild, due 30 Nov)
